entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-gv3v-2cpp-3pmq: Keycloak logs sensitive headers
entry.content:
Keycloak logs sensitive headers

Aliases: CVE-2025-11537

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • org.keycloak:keycloak-quarkus-server — fixed in 26.5.6

A flaw was found in Keycloak. When the logging format is configured to a verbose, user-supplied pattern (such as the pre-defined 'long' pattern), sensitive headers including Authorization and Cookie are disclosed to the logs in cleartext. An attacker with read access to the log files can extract these credentials (e.g., bearer tokens, session cookies) and use them to impersonate users, leading to a full account compromise. Patches are available, see: - https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/releases/tag/26.4.11 - https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/releases/tag/26.5.6 - https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/releases/tag/26.6.0

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-f5p5-6xmx-p252: Keycloak vulnerable to authorization bypass via incorrect uri comparison
entry.content:
Keycloak vulnerable to authorization bypass via incorrect uri comparison

Aliases: BIT-keycloak-2026-9800, CVE-2026-9800

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • org.keycloak:keycloak-services — fixed in 26.6.4
  • org.keycloak:keycloak-policy-enforcer — fixed in 26.0.10

### Description A flaw was found in Keycloak Policy Enforcer. This vulnerability allows any authenticated user to bypass all authorization policies, including role, scope, and User-Managed Access (UMA) permission checks. By including the configured access-denied page path within a request URL, either as a path segment or a query parameter, an attacker can gain unauthorized access to protected resources.

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-v3f7-2p4r-mwfw: Keycloak vulnerable to cross-site scripting (xss) via case-insensitive uri validation bypass
entry.content:
Keycloak vulnerable to cross-site scripting (xss) via case-insensitive uri validation bypass

Aliases: BIT-keycloak-2026-9086, CVE-2026-9086

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • org.keycloak:keycloak-services — fixed in 26.6.4

### Description A flaw was found in Keycloak. A remote attacker with administrative privileges, specifically those with `manage-client` permission or access to client registration endpoints, could bypass client Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) validation. This is achieved by registering a malicious client with a specially crafted redirect URI using a case-insensitive `javascript:` or `data:` scheme. This Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability allows for arbitrary code execution in the Keycloak origin when a victim clicks the crafted link, such as in the logout flow or the Admin Console.

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-9jrw-8xf7-xqhq: Keycloak vulnerable to information disclosure through arbitrary filesystem path probing
entry.content:
Keycloak vulnerable to information disclosure through arbitrary filesystem path probing

Aliases: BIT-keycloak-2026-9083, CVE-2026-9083

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • org.keycloak:keycloak-services — fixed in 26.6.4

### Description A flaw was found in Keycloak. A realm administrator with the "manage-realm" role can exploit this vulnerability by submitting an arbitrary filesystem path as a keystore parameter when creating a key provider component. This allows the administrator to probe arbitrary filesystem paths, determining which files exist and are readable by the Keycloak process. This information disclosure could be used to identify high-value targets for follow-on attacks.

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-w3p3-7cjg-vgfw: Keycloak allows unauthorized access to resources via uma permission ticket bypass
entry.content:
Keycloak allows unauthorized access to resources via uma permission ticket bypass

Aliases: BIT-keycloak-2026-9799, CVE-2026-9799

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N

Affected:

  • org.keycloak:keycloak-services — fixed in 26.6.4

### Description A flaw was found in org.keycloak.authorization. An authenticated user with a granted User-Managed Access (UMA) permission ticket for one resource can exploit this by using a specific permission request prefix to bypass per-resource access control. This allows the user to gain unauthorized access to all resources of that type within the same resource server, even if they do not have a ticket for those specific resources. This vulnerability requires the resource server to be configured in PERMISSIVE policy enforcement mode and affects typed resources with ownerManagedAccess enabled, where no explicit policy protects the resource type. The primary consequence is unauthorized information disclosure or modification of resources.

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-r7rc-c989-86g6: Keycloak: Attacker can re-enable and take over disabled clients via registration access token
entry.content:
Keycloak: Attacker can re-enable and take over disabled clients via registration access token

Aliases: BIT-keycloak-2026-9705, CVE-2026-9705

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N

Affected:

  • org.keycloak:keycloak-services — fixed in 26.6.4

### Description A flaw was found in Keycloak's client registration service. A remote attacker, possessing a previously issued Registration Access Token (RAT), could exploit this vulnerability to re-enable a client that an administrator had explicitly disabled. This bypasses security controls, allowing the attacker to reset the client's secret and potentially regain privileged API access. The primary impact includes unauthorized information disclosure and potential integrity compromise.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-ccrj-gw8r-854m: opentelemetry-java: Quadratic CPU consumption in W3C tracestate parsing

opentelemetry-java: Quadratic CPU consumption in W3C tracestate parsing

Aliases: CVE-2026-118259

Affected:

  • io.opentelemetry:opentelemetry-api — fixed in 1.67.0

### Summary OpenTelemetry Java's W3C trace-context propagator permits excessive CPU consumption when extracting crafted `tracestate` headers, potentially leading to denial of service. entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-r9pv-5rpp-vm8g: OpenAM Unauthenticated Session Hijacking via Information Exposure in CDCServlet
entry.content:
OpenAM Unauthenticated Session Hijacking via Information Exposure in CDCServlet

Aliases: CVE-2026-45049

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • org.openidentityplatform.openam:openam-federation — fixed in 16.1.1

## Summary **Description** An Information Exposure Through Sent Data (CWE-201) issue in OpenAM's Cross-Domain Single Sign-On (CDSSO) servlet allows a logged-in user's raw OpenAM session token to be POSTed to an attacker-controlled URL. This impacts OpenAM Community Edition through version 16.0.6. This issue was patched in version 16.1.1. An attacker who can induce a logged-in victim to visit a crafted URL may receive the victim's session credential, which could enable session hijacking. ## Impact OpenAM deployments through version 16.0.6 that have CDSSO enabled are potentially affected. The CDSSO component is commonly enabled in multi-domain deployments. Exploitation requires user interaction — an authenticated user must be induced to visit an attacker-crafted URL — and is further gate…
